ordered_diagnoses: Bile duct stricture due to chemotherapy

s1.syndrome_frame: Cholestatic jaundice with bile duct strictures and dilatations in a patient with a history of chemotherapy
salient_findings: Wall thickening of the extrahepatic and intrahepatic bile ducts and of the gallbladder
key_facts: Metastatic to paraaortic and left supraclavicular lymph nodes
Admitted for marked elevation of liver enzymes
Abdominal ultrasonography showed wall thickening of the extrahepatic and intrahepatic bile ducts and of the gallbladder
Contrast-enhanced CT confirmed wall thickening of both extrahepatic and intrahepatic bile ducts
Biopsy of the common bile duct showed no malignant cells
Bile cytology was negative for malignancy

raw.rationale: The patient's recent treatment with paclitaxel for 63 days, followed by the development of marked elevation of liver enzymes and wall thickening of the extrahepatic and intrahepatic bile ducts, suggests a drug-induced cause. The absence of malignant cells in the biopsy and negative bile cytology further support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Primary sclerosing cholangitis
rejected.why: No prior history or evidence of inflammatory bowel disease, which is often associated with primary sclerosing cholangitis

rejected.label: IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis
rejected.why: No mention of elevated IgG4 levels or other characteristic features of IgG4-related disease

rejected.label: Bile duct stricture due to chemotherapy
rejected.why: While chemotherapy can cause bile duct strictures, the specific temporal relationship with paclitaxel administration makes sclerosing cholangitis due to paclitaxel a more precise diagnosis

rejected.label: Cholangiocarcinoma
rejected.why: Biopsy and bile cytology were negative for malignancy, making cholangiocarcinoma less likely
